tagline: Out of the town that melted a king into bullets.
intro: Route 63 comes up from the Morris line to Litchfield's green, where US 202 crosses, and carries on north out of town. Route 118 leaves the green eastward, crosses the Bantam River, and meets Route 254, which runs off southeast to the village of Northfield. Each stays scenic for a few miles.

The green began in 1720 as common pasture, with the first meetinghouse on it by 1723 and the county courthouse by 1751. The grazing ended after the Revolution, the ground served for military parades, and in 1836 the town made it a park.

moments.title: Tapping Reeve House and Law School
moments.text: On South Street stands the one-room school Tapping Reeve built beside his house in 1784, which taught more than 1,100 students, Aaron Burr and John C. Calhoun among them.

moments.title: Litchfield
moments.text: In 1776 a lead statue of George III, pulled down in New York, was hauled here and melted into bullets in Oliver Wolcott's house by his daughter and sister.

moments.title: Northfield
moments.text: The Northfield Knife Company worked here from 1858 to 1926, and its foundations still sit across the street from Knife Shop Dam.
